summary: Examples of template: setting owner/group/mode with octal or symbolic modes, OS-specific source with an SELinux type, CRLF output, validating sudoers with visudo, and safely updating sshd_config with validation and backup.
questions: How do I template sshd_config without locking myself out?
How do I deploy a sudoers file with validation?
How do I choose a template file based on OS family?
How do I create a DOS-style file from a template?

answer_card.title: template examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.template:
    src: /mytemplates/foo.j2
    dest: /etc/file.conf
    owner: bin
    group: wheel
    mode: '0644'
- ansible.builtin.template:
    src: named.conf_{{ ansible_os_family }}.j2
    dest: /etc/named.conf
    setype: named_conf_t
- ansible.builtin.template: {src: config.ini.j2, dest: /share/windows/config.ini, newline_sequence: '\r\n'}
- ansible.builtin.template: {src: /mine/sudoers, dest: /etc/sudoers, validate: /usr/sbin/visudo -cf %s}
- ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/ssh/sshd_config.j2
    dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
    mode: '0600'
    validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
    backup: yes
```
